A TREND RANGE IS WITHDRAWN HERE, deliberately. An earlier version of this row moved brick to the ends of its band in FY2023-24 only (7.65 to 12.60 Gg) and divided by the UNCHANGED FY2015-16 total, reporting a decline of 29 to 62 per cent. That is not a range of trends: it is one endpoint varied against a fixed denominator, and the band does not even exist for FY2015-16. A trend range needs a coherent scenario applied at BOTH endpoints - the same coal account, fuel-quality history, kiln history, allocation and coverage in each year - and that is what the scenario work owes. Until then the honest statement is the per-year band above and nothing multiplied out of it

the CCAC's own estimate is a FLAT 13,000 kt of brick-kiln coal in every one of the nine years - above every official value and far above the FY2023-24 trough of 1,129. On that reading brick contributes no trend at all and Lahore's decline is whatever the other streams do. NEVER added to the booked change: it is a single cross-section, not an annual indicator, which is why outputs/pakemis_industrial_coal_decision.csv leaves the official column booked

POWER SO2 IS IN THIS CURVE, AND THIS ROW SAID THE OPPOSITE UNTIL rc64. It read 'power SO2 is typed NE (uncontrolled-screening-only) in all nine periods, so it has never been in this curve in any year' - true when written and false from rc60, when the oil and diesel fleet was admitted on a reviewed register and rc61 placed it. The coverage matrix now types power SO2 as E in all nine periods. Lahore's power row is ONE station, Kohinoor Energy, whose published SO2 equals its own row in data/activity/power/power_so2_admission.csv to six decimals, metered from NEPRA fuel quantities in five of the nine years. It contributes 8.598 Gg of the 17.456 Gg fall - the largest single sector - so a reader who took this row at its word was missing half the curve. What the row still establishes is unchanged: the sector coverage matrix is identical across the nine periods, so no part of the change is coverage moving
